scope: Historical reported results; not regenerated by code-release checks. Table captions retain manuscript LaTeX references.

tables.label: tab:followup-p1
tables.caption_latex: Larger harmful-keep assay. Counts retain all 232 behavior IDs, including copyright requests. The checkpoint and scorer differ from the primary experiment. ``Active'' means nonzero harmful intervention.

tables.label: tab:followup-categories
tables.caption_latex: HarmBench category-wise refusal counts on the larger assay. ``No veto'' denotes thresholded routing. $\Delta$ compares the vetoed policy with the base within each category.

tables.label: tab:followup-models
tables.caption_latex: Base$\to$RP refusal counts from two open-weight judges. Harmful denominators are 90; edit denominators are 36. ``Identical'' is the number of exactly equal harmful decoded strings, out of 90. Both judges have zero paired harmful-refusal label flips in every row, while edit refusal remains high and its change depends on model and judge.

tables.label: tab:followup-rp-quality
tables.caption_latex: Five-way edit-response labels, base$\to$RP counts, $n=36$ per model. These labels are a different endpoint from the binary refusal rubric in Table~\ref{tab:followup-models}. All five categories are retained.

tables.label: tab:followup-baselines
tables.caption_latex: Additional baseline quality measurements. Arrows show base$\to$edited counts. Edit F/H/B lists edited useful reframes/actionable assistance/broken outputs. ``Unknown'' gives base$\to$edited unparseable harmful labels, which remain in the denominators; all edit labels parse. Q14, G2, and Q7 denote Qwen2.5-14B, Gemma-2-2B, and Qwen2.5-7B. These are unmatched generation protocols and capacities, not a ranking against the primary RP row.

tables.label: tab:followup-xstest
tables.caption_latex: Additional same-source XSTest test, six examples per bucket. Refusal uses markers. The harmful slice is saturated and too small to rule out dataset-source confounding.

tables.label: app:oracle-provenance
tables.caption_latex: Tuning ranges and selection rules for matched-protocol controls. All rows use the local SALAD/Alpaca/HarmBench split, greedy decoding, and the edit-base-refusal filter. One-direction baselines fit a single activation direction, then sweep only intervention scale and optional routing policy. \method{} additionally trains a router and residual controller; oracle rows are diagnostics and are not deployable. The comparison is matched-protocol, not equal-capacity hyperparameter tuning.
